Q: In JavaScript, what exactly does the array method map do, and how is it used? A:

There's the notion of a "mapping" of one thing to another. Maps/Dictionaries represent this key/value pairing in that sense (a "mapping" K -> V of keys to values). However, to .map() a list of items is to iterate over each item, applying the mapping function (the K -> V above), and returning the list of results from said operation. So if your "mapping function" was map_func = i => i + 1, and you have an array [1,2,3], then [1,2,3].map(map_func) will return [2,3,4]. You can map things into new objects, or function call results, etc. This concept goes well beyond Javascript as well.

Q: What does \ means in programming? A:

It looks almost certainly like Visual Basic with the use of End If, Set, ^ for power...

In VB \ is an integer division operator so Temperature \ 100 means taking the integer part of the result Temperature / 100

In Visual BASIC (and some other BASIC dialects) the backslash is used as an operator symbol to indicate integer division. This rounds toward zero.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backslash#Programming_languages

Q: Writing to file from console produces whitespace A:

Using the size of the buffer as the size for WriteToFile will always write a full 50 bytes; it's like C fwrite, taking a pointer and length, so it works on arbitrary bytes, not just 0-terminated C strings.
At best you could make the trailing bytes all zeros, but the file length will still be 50 instead of 4.

ReadString returns the actual length read (in EAX), so use that as the size to write. It's guaranteed to not be longer than the buffer size; if the user types more characters before pressing enter, they're ignored.

Search for ReadString PROC in the library source to see comments describing the function: https://github.com/miguelmota/x86-assembly-examples/blob/master/IrvineExamplesVS2012/Examples/Lib32/Irvine32_Library/Irvine32.asm

Str_trim only removes trailing chars from a 0-terminated C string by replacing the first of the repeated trailing bytes with a 0 byte. e.g. Hello### turns into Hello\0##. (Which as a 0-terminated C-string is just "Hello", but the last two # bytes are still there in memory.)

https://csie.ntu.edu.tw/~acpang/course/asm_2004/slides/chapt_09.pdf shows the actual implementation. (Actually the old implementation which uses std / repne scasb and returns with DF=1 which makes rep-string ops go backwards in memory. This ironically violates the normal calling conventions despite Irvine32 functions normally saving/restoring even ECX and EDX, and even EAX if they don't have a return value. I assume that was the reason for the rewrite. Unfortunately the current version uses the slow loop instruction instead of dec ecx/jne, and does a clunky load into AL and compare against function arg on the stack instead of cmp [edi], al; pretty bad example of how to write asm.)

If you still write the whole buffer to the file, all the other whitespace is still there, plus the zero byte.
